messages.content:
You review lab-result summaries written by FOXO's Doctor agent for a busy human clinician.

You will see the lab data the agent was given (abnormal results, sample quality issues, unreadable items) and the agent's summary and follow-ups. Judge how useful the summary is to the clinician. Do not judge medical correctness here; other checks cover that.

For each criterion, first write one or two sentences of reasoning, then set passed to true or false.

Criteria (use these ids exactly, one entry each):
- leads_with_priority: The most important finding comes first. Critical values, if any, are stated before routine ones.
- concise: A busy clinician can read the summary in under a minute. No padding, no repeated content.
- actionable: The clinician can see what to do next (follow-ups, referrals or repeat tests).
- flags_limitations: Sample quality issues and unreadable or missing results are mentioned when the lab data has them. Pass if there are none.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"CriterionVerdict": {"properties": {"criterion": {"title": "Criterion", "type": "string"}, "reasoning": {"title": "Reasoning", "type": "string"}, "passed": {"title": "Passed", "type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["criterion", "reasoning", "passed"], "title": "CriterionVerdict", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"criteria": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/CriterionVerdict"}, "title": "Criteria", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["criteria"], "title": "JudgeOutput", "type": "object"}

Lab data given to the agent:
- Abnormal results: vitamin_d 14.0 ng/mL (low)
- Sample quality issues: none
- Unreadable items: none

Summary for clinician:
- Vitamin D (25-OH) is low at 14.0 ng/mL (ref 30.0–100.0 ng/mL); all other reported biomarkers (CRP, ALT, haemoglobin) are within reference ranges.
- Member has requested vitamin D tablets; a draft has been prepared for your review and approval — no prescription has been issued.
- No medications, allergies or known interactions on file; no sample quality issues reported.

Recommended follow-ups:
- General physician review of vitamin D (25-OH) result at 14.0 ng/mL to confirm supplementation approach and any further testing.
- Repeat vitamin D (25-OH) test after a course of supplementation to assess response.
- Repeat lipid panel, fasting glucose and HbA1c are not available in this report — suggest ordering if clinically indicated.

response: {"criteria": [{"criterion": "leads_with_priority", "reasoning": "The only abnormal finding (low vitamin D at 14.0 ng/mL) is stated in the very first bullet, before routine information about the prescription draft and member history. No critical values were present, so the ordering is appropriate.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "concise", "reasoning": "The summary is three short bullets plus three follow-ups, easily readable in well under a minute. The vitamin D value is repeated once in the follow-ups, but this is minor and does not add meaningful length or padding.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "actionable", "reasoning": "Next steps are clear: the clinician is told a prescription draft awaits their review and approval, a GP review is recommended to confirm the supplementation approach, and a repeat test after supplementation is suggested. The clinician knows exactly what to do.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "flags_limitations", "reasoning": "The lab data contains no sample quality issues and no unreadable or missing items, so this criterion passes by default. The summary even explicitly confirms no sample quality issues were reported.", "passed": true}]}
